# iOS App Development Guide (Swift/SwiftUI)

`ios-app/`, SwiftUI. Structure et rôle dans l'ensemble : [ARCHITECTURE.md](../ARCHITECTURE.md).
Commandes : [mise.instructions.md](mise.instructions.md) · CI : [ci.instructions.md](ci.instructions.md) · Règles de
code : [CODING_STANDARDS.md](../CODING_STANDARDS.md) › iOS.

## Generated files (CRITICAL)

- **`project.yml` is the source of truth.** `ArcaneExchange.xcodeproj/` is git-ignored and regenerated by XcodeGen —
  **never edit `project.pbxproj`**. `ArcaneExchange/Info.plist` _is_ committed but also regenerated, from the
  `info.properties` block: plist keys go in `project.yml`.
- A target-level setting in `project.yml` **wins over** `Config/*.xcconfig`, so per-target values belong in
  `settings.base`; shared values in `Shared.xcconfig` + `Dev`/`Release.xcconfig`.
- The system accent is the `Primary` color asset, through `ASSETCATALOG_COMPILER_GLOBAL_ACCENT_COLOR_NAME` in
  `project.yml` — rename one, rename the other.
- `//` starts a comment in an xcconfig: a URL must be written `http:/$()/host` (see `Dev.xcconfig`).
- **Xcode 26 required locally**, and the `metal` compiler is a downloadable component: a fresh machine builds only
  after `xcodebuild -downloadComponent MetalToolchain` (a few GB), otherwise `cannot execute tool 'metal'`.

## API Client

- `APIClient/` sources are generated by `mise run generate-api-client` (direct `swift-openapi-generator` CLI, **no
  build plugin** — a symlink into `Sources/` broke Portainer's git checkout, which refuses repos with symlinks) and
  **committed**. `APIClient.swift` is intentionally empty.
- The `APIClient` target builds with `-suppress-warnings` (`Package.swift`): the generator writes a `public import`
  per module in every file, one `UnusedImportAccess` warning each. It mutes **every** warning of the module, so keep
  hand-written code out of it — and check `swift build` without the flag after bumping `swift-openapi-*`.
- New code goes through `APIClientFactory` (`ArcaneExchangeCore/Networking/`, ADR-0020): view models take `any APIProtocol` in their
  initializer (views read it from `\.api`), read only the success of an `Output` (`.ok`, `.noContent`) and catch with
  `APIError.read`. Tests use `FakeAPI` (`TestSupport/`). The app builds its client once, in `ArcaneExchangeApp`.
- `APIClientFactory` takes the base URL as a closure (`AppConfig.apiBaseURL` by default), read on each request: the
  base URL is editable at runtime, so never capture it once.

## Targets and test bundles

- `ArcaneExchangeCore/` (framework, `import ArcaneExchangeCore`) holds everything that is not a screen; `ArcaneExchange/` holds the
  screens. Declarations the app, the extension or the tests use are `package`, never `public` (ADR 0025).
- `ArcaneExchangeCoreTests/` is the only test target: it tests `ArcaneExchangeCore/` and runs with no host app (no `TEST_HOST`), so
  nothing in it can `@testable import ArcaneExchange`. Logic worth testing never stays in a screen file: it goes
  into `ArcaneExchangeCore/` (`AppRouter`, `OwnedEntryLabel`, `TradeSteps`…). `TestSupport/` (`FakeAPI`, fixtures) is
  compiled into the bundle: write its fixtures against `APIClient` types.
- A test never reads `Bundle.main` in `ArcaneExchangeCoreTests`: it is the test runner, not the app. Resources resolve in
  `Palette.bundle`; `AppConfig` and `SharedContainer` take an injected `info:` dictionary.

## Home-screen widgets

- The `ArcaneExchangeWidgets` extension holds only its entry point and `WidgetSession`: everything else it runs lives
  in the `ArcaneExchangeCore` framework (ADR 0025), which it links and the app embeds. A type the widgets need goes into
  `ArcaneExchangeCore/`, with no `sources` line to keep. Keep `ArcaneExchangeCore` free of screens and of `NukeUI` /
  `ClerkKitUI` imports.
- Clerk and Nuke are linked through `APIClient`'s dynamic products `ClerkKitShared` and `NukeShared` (plus `NukeUI`
  in the app), never as plain `ClerkKit` / `Nuke` products: Xcode would link the UI libraries statically into the
  app with a second copy of each core library, whose singletons the framework never configures (`Clerk.shared`
  traps at launch). The app embeds them (`embed: true`): unlike automatic products, an explicitly dynamic product
  is not copied otherwise, and only the simulator finds it in DerivedData. `mise run check-ios-linking` (also in
  CI) fails when a module is linked twice or an `@rpath` library is missing from the bundle.
- The widget views live in `ArcaneExchangeCore/HomeWidgets/`, not in the extension, so tests and previews can render them.
- Everything shared with the app is in `SharedContainer`: the App Group (API base URL, last snapshots)
  and the Keychain group holding the Clerk session. Both are declared in the two targets'
  `entitlements` in `project.yml` — rename one side, rename the other. Clerk is configured through
  `ClerkSetup` in both processes; never call `Clerk.configure` directly.
- The app reloads the widgets itself (`HomeWidgetReload`) after anything that changes what they show;
  `HomeWidgetSchedule` only covers the app being closed. The authenticated API client does it for every
  mutation that changes what a widget shows, from the operation table of `WidgetsReloadMiddleware` (any
  HTTP response, an error included). Rating a trade and the trade settings are deliberately absent: no
  widget shows them. A new mutation that changes what a widget shows adds a line to that table. View
  models do not call `HomeWidgetReload`, with one named exception: `ImportViewModel` at the end of an
  import (not a mutation: the server answers 202 first). `reloadAll` stays for sign-in, sign-out and the
  app leaving the foreground.
- Widget taps open `arcane-exchange://` links (`HomeWidgetLink`), routed by `AppRouter`.

## Runtime configuration

`AppConfig` reads `API_BASE_URL` and `CLERK_PUBLISHABLE_KEY` from `Info.plist` (fed by the xcconfigs at build time).
The base URL is overridable at runtime from Settings ▸ Arcane Exchange — `UserDefaults` key `api_base_url`, declared
in `Settings.bundle/Root.plist`: **keep both in sync, they share no symbol**. Debug builds point at
`http://localhost:3000/api/v1` — the Nuxt dev server, which proxies the API and serves `/card-images` — and
`Local.xcconfig`'s Clerk key must be the instance the backend validates against.

`Config/Local.xcconfig` is git-ignored and holds the two per-developer values (`DEVELOPMENT_TEAM`,
`CLERK_PUBLISHABLE_KEY`) — copy `Local.xcconfig.example` on a fresh checkout. It is pulled in with `#include?`, so
builds and CI pass without it; only sign-in needs the real key.
